quote: But a deeper vengeance is taken on fiercer foes and on those that are false as well as on those who have done greater wrongs, as was the case with the Midianites. For they had made many of the Jewish people to sin through their women. For this reason the anger of the Lord was poured out upon the people of our fathers. Thus it came about that Moses when victorious allowed none of them to live.
source_title: On the Duties of the Clergy 1.29.139

quote: In the passages above, the sons of Israel committed fornication with the women of the Midianites, and this was a stumbling-block to the sons of Israel, in which they offended the Lord and provoked to anger the Holy One of Israel. Now therefore, after Israel had suffered what it suffered, "the Lord spoke," it says, "to Moses, saying: Avenge the vengeance of the sons of Israel upon the Midianites, and afterward you shall be added to your people." Therefore, as for the stumbling-blocks that had befallen the Israelites, since they had befallen them through the treachery of the Midianites — for they themselves had suborned the women who were to deceive them, so that they might sin before the Lord — those men indeed suffered punishment for their sin, yet more moderately and more sparingly, whereas these, who were the cause of their sinning, are subjected to a far more severe vengeance. Whence…

After these things Moses spoke to the people, saying: "Arm men of yourselves and make war against Midian, to render vengeance from the Lord upon Midian; a thousand from a tribe and a thousand from a tribe; from all the tribes of Israel send men to make war." Attend to the reading; for the mind must be directed not only to the hearing of words, but to the consideration of the realities. Recall the things past, hear the things present, mark the things that follow. Compare the earlier things with the later, and contemplate the magnificence of the divine powers. The sons of Israel some time ago had been six hundred thousand armed men who had gone forth against Midian, and all these were conquered, because sin was in them. But now the Midianites, the victors, who had put to flight six hundred thousand, are conquered by twelve thousand, that you may know that Israel conquers not in a…

Therefore twelve thousand engage against the Midianites, and "they slay," it says, "all their males; and their kings and Balaam, the son of Beor, they slew with the sword together with the rest of their wounded." That which in the passages above we were inquiring — how it could be proved from the Scriptures that the women of the Midianites, who deceived the sons of Israel into fornicating, had been suborned by the counsel of Balaam — this present passage of Scripture evidently shows, saying that he was slain by the sword as the author of the scandal that was brought upon the sons of Israel. And it is said of him in what follows still more evidently in this way: "and Moses said to them: why have you preserved every woman alive? For it is they who, according to the word of Balaam, made the sons of Israel apostates." And the kings of the Midianites are also slain, and those who were…

But the divine Scripture was also careful to record their names. "Evi," it says, "and Rekem and Zur and Hur and Reba." These are they who reign among the Midianites, whom everyone who serves God as a soldier ought to overcome and utterly to destroy. For Evi is interpreted "beastly" or "wild." And how will you be able to please Him who has approved you, if you do not cut off from yourself and utterly destroy beastly and wild ways? How will you be able to attain to the beatitude of the meek, unless first you slay Evi and hand over to death the wildness of all anger? I think that the divine Scripture did not narrate these names for the sake of history, but fitted them for the sake of causes and realities. For do you suppose there would have been anyone so foolish as to impose on his son the name "Beastly"? But I judge rather that the divine word looked to the instruction of souls, wishing…

The soothsayer Balaam set up a scandal for the people of Israel when he went to meet their warriors, not with men in armor but with women arrayed in all their finery. He hoped to make the men drop their arms for debauchery, change their triumph into disgrace, bring the avengers of guilt into guilt themselves and—to put it briefly—to profane all their holiness into depravity. As a result of it all, when Moses was meting out punishment, he sentenced Balaam thus: "Kill Balaam the soothsayer, because he set up a stumbling block before the children of Israel."

The same angel, however, said to the Virgin Mary, "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with you"; the one who will be in you is already with you. "Blessed are you among women." Holy Scripture bears witness to the fact that in the proper usage of the Hebrew language all females are habitually called women; in case some of you perhaps may be astonished and scandalized, if you are not used to hearing the Scriptures. There's a place in the Scriptures where the Lord says openly, "Set apart the women who have not known man." In any case, call to mind those origins of ours; when Eve was made from the man's side, what does Scripture say? "He removed a rib from him and built it into a woman." She is already called a woman, taken indeed from the man but not yet united to the man. So now, when you hear from the angel, "Blessed are you among women," take it in such a way, as if it were saying, in our…

Finally, in the present reading, Eleazar the priest is not written as speaking to all the people, but only to those who return from the battle. For it says: "and Eleazar the priest said to the men of valor, who were returning from the battle." You see, then, how the word of God speaks to the men of valor. For men of valor are they who go forth to war. But if anyone is unwilling to fight and to be a soldier, if anyone is unwilling to have the contest of divine studies and of abstinence, this man is unwilling to fulfill that which the Apostle said: "but he who contends in the contest is continent from all things." He, then, who does not contend in the contest and is not continent from all things, nor wishes to be exercised in the word of God and to meditate on the law of the Lord day and night, this man, even if he be called a man, cannot nevertheless be called a man of valor. But this…

Therefore it says: "This is the justification of the law which the Lord established for Moses: besides gold and silver and bronze and iron and lead and tin, every thing that passes through fire, pass it through fire and it shall be cleansed, but it shall also be purified in the water of purification; all things whatsoever that do not pass through fire shall pass through water. And you shall wash your garments on the seventh day, and you shall be clean; and after these things you shall enter into the camps." You see how everyone who has gone out of the battle of this life needs purification. And if this is so, that I may dare to say something according to the authority of Scripture, everyone who goes out of this life cannot be clean. For consider diligently what the text of the history indicates. These men went out to fight for the sons of Israel, they slew the Midianites; and in slaying…

Therefore, by the command of the Lord, the wars against the Midianites were carried through by the sons of Israel; abundant spoils are brought back from them, an immense weight of gold and silver and of the other movable goods, a very great number of beasts and of captives. But since among the Israelites all these things are reckoned unclean, a purification suited to each several thing is applied; and those things indeed which consist of metals, fire purifies, but those which are more fragile and do not bear the fire are commanded to be purified by water. Therefore from all the spoils two equal parts are made, that one may be of those who had gone forth to war and the other of those who had remained in the camps. They are also commanded to offer from these into the gifts of God: those indeed who had gone forth to war, one head out of five hundred; but those who had remained in the…

But let us see what the spiritual sense indicates in these things. In the people of God there are certain ones, as the Apostle says, who serve God as soldiers — those without doubt who do not entangle themselves in secular affairs; and these are they who go forth to war and fight against the enemy nations and against the spiritual wickednesses on behalf of the rest of the people and on behalf of those who are weaker, whether by age or by sex or by resolve. And these fight with prayers and fastings, with righteousness and piety, with meekness and chastity and all the virtues of continence, fortified as with weapons of war; and when they have returned to the camps as victors, even the unwarlike enjoy their labors, and those who either are not called to the fight or cannot go out. Yet it must be known that all things that are taken from these nations are unclean; and perhaps everything…

That there are differences of progress and of merits among the people of the faithful, anyone who attends more carefully to the reading will discover in many places in the divine volumes. And we gather this no less from the present reading also, from what is written: "And there came to Moses all who had been appointed leaders throughout the tribes in the army, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds. And they said to Moses: We your servants have gathered the sum total of our men of war, and not one of us was missing; and we have offered a gift to the Lord, each man whatever vessel of gold he found, a collar or a bracelet or a ring or an armlet or a little chain, to make propitiation for ourselves before the Lord." The chosen leaders, then, who had been appointed over the army, speak to Moses and, for their deeds well done, offer gifts to God, saying: "We are your servants,…

Consider now the state of the present age, and see all things filled with wars and all human life hard pressed by invisible battles and by the assaults of demons, but that among the people of God there are certain ones so strong in faith and armed with virtues that against enemies of this kind they daily wage wars and, always standing ready in battle array, guard from the ambushes of the enemy not only themselves but also the rest who cannot fight, whether by reason of sex or of age or of the condition of servitude, fortifying them by the word of teaching and by the example of their life and by the diligence of their admonitions; provided, however, that faith be not lacking to them. For whether warriors or unfit for war, it is impossible to be saved without faith.
